description: A comprehensive study of dietary components essential for growth, energy, and health maintenance in living organisms. It covers macronutrients, micronutrients, and detailed descriptions of diseases caused by their deficiencies.

sections.title: Basic Principles of Nutrition
sections.description: Overview of major nutrients required for body growth and maintenance.

key_concepts.explanation: The process by which organisms take in food and utilize it for energy, growth, and tissue repair.
The primary and quickest source of energy for the body, composed of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen in a 1:2:1 ratio.
Complex organic compounds made of amino acids, essential for cell repair and growth. They are often referred to as 'body-building foods'.
The most concentrated source of energy. They help in regulating body temperature and protecting internal organs.

important_facts.fact: Severe protein deficiency in the diet causes diseases like Kwashiorkor and Marasmus, predominantly in children.

sections.title: Fat-Soluble Vitamins
sections.description: Vitamins that dissolve in fats and are stored in the liver and adipose tissues.

key_associations.associated_with: Chemical Name: Retinol | Disease: Night Blindness, Xerophthalmia
key_associations.extra_info: Crucial for vision and immunity. Rich sources include carrots, spinach, and papaya.

key_associations.associated_with: Chemical Name: Calciferol | Disease: Rickets (in children), Osteomalacia (in adults)
key_associations.extra_info: Known as the 'Sunshine Vitamin'. Essential for calcium absorption in the bones.

key_associations.associated_with: Chemical Name: Tocopherol | Disease: Infertility, Muscle weakness
key_associations.extra_info: Popularly known as the 'Beauty Vitamin' and acts as a powerful antioxidant protecting cells from damage.

key_associations.associated_with: Chemical Name: Phylloquinone | Disease: Hemorrhage / Non-clotting of blood
key_associations.extra_info: Essential for blood coagulation to prevent excessive bleeding from wounds.

sections.title: Water-Soluble Vitamins
sections.description: Vitamins that dissolve in water, are not stored in the body, and are excreted through urine.

key_associations.extra_info: Deficiency is common in populations consuming a diet primarily of highly polished rice.

key_associations.associated_with: Chemical Name: Niacin | Disease: Pellagra (4D Syndrome)
key_associations.extra_info: The 4D Syndrome stands for Dermatitis, Diarrhea, Dementia, and Death.

key_associations.associated_with: Chemical Name: Folic Acid | Disease: Megaloblastic Anemia
key_associations.extra_info: Crucial during pregnancy for the proper development of the fetal nervous system.

key_associations.associated_with: Chemical Name: Cyanocobalamin | Disease: Pernicious Anemia
key_associations.extra_info: The only vitamin containing the transition metal cobalt. It is naturally absent in plant-based foods.

key_associations.associated_with: Chemical Name: Ascorbic Acid | Disease: Scurvy
key_associations.extra_info: Destroyed easily by heat and washing. Aids in wound healing and is abundantly found in citrus fruits like amla and lemon.

sections.title: Essential Minerals and Deficiencies
sections.description: Inorganic elements required for proper bodily functions and diseases linked to their lack.

key_associations.extra_info: Essential for the formation of hemoglobin in red blood cells, which transports oxygen throughout the body.
Required for the synthesis of thyroxine hormone by the thyroid gland to regulate metabolism.

key_associations.associated_with: Disease: Osteoporosis, Weak bones and teeth
key_associations.extra_info: Calcium is also highly essential for blood clotting and proper muscle contraction.

key_associations.associated_with: Disease: Low Blood Pressure, Muscle cramps
key_associations.extra_info: Responsible for maintaining bodily water balance and transmitting nerve impulses.

sections.title: Important Exam-Oriented Facts
sections.description: Direct, high-yield facts related to nutrition frequently asked in competitive exams.

important_facts.fact: Fats provide the highest calorific value (approx. 9.3 kcal/g), whereas carbohydrates and proteins provide about 4.1 kcal/g.
Milk is not considered a completely balanced food because it naturally lacks Vitamin C and Iron.
The term 'Vitamin' was first coined by the Polish biochemist Casimir Funk in 1912.
Vitamins cannot be synthesized by the human body (with the exception of Vitamins D and K) and must be obtained from dietary sources.
Fish liver oil is an excellent and concentrated natural source of both Vitamin A and Vitamin D.
